1.1: 1.1 Preface. RABANUS, Exposition on the book of Judith, vol. 3. It is asked at what time and under what kings the history of Judith took place, etc., down to unless perhaps it be said that Cambyses, who is said to have attacked the neighboring nations and conquered Egypt, since the kingdom of the Assyrians and Persians was one, defeated and subjected to his rule some king named Arphaxad resisting in Media. Arphaxad. RABANUS, as above. Mystically, by Arphaxad the proud are expressed, whose efforts and labor, carried on in the vastness of swelling and elation, easily fall into the power of Nebuchadnezzar, that is of the devil: for he is king over all the children of pride. Which he called. Which is the metropolis of the province of Media, which Deioces king of the Medes founded, but Arphaxad wondrously enlarged, as Daniel the prophet, according to Josephus, under King Darius built in the same city of Media a very splendid mausoleum with wondrous art, which on whatever day it is seen is thought to have been just built, so new is the beauty and so solid the material. There to this day the kings of the Persians and Medes are buried, and the care of this is committed to a priest who is a Jew. In glory. These in chariots and these in horses, etc. But God cast the chariot of Pharaoh and his army into the sea: therefore he who glories, let him glory in the Lord.
1.6: 1.6 In the great plain. RABANUS, as above. By the names of places, etc., down to and finally conceded the victories to the Chaldeans or Assyrians. Then was exalted. When the devil subjects a multitude of the lost to his will, his heart is lifted up, assigning it to his own power, not to divine permission: and the more he burns for the destruction of very many lost ones, the more he sees himself prevail over some by wicked suggestion, whence it follows. And he sent to all. RABANUS, ibid. The devil sends envoys through the various provinces, etc., down to hence: All with one mind gainsaid, etc.
1.12: 1.12 Then Nebuchadnezzar was angry. The devil, blinded by his own pride, arrogates to himself the empire of the whole world, contending to draw men away from the worship of piety and make them sharers of his impiety: who exulting in the power of the kingdom says: I will ascend into heaven, and I will set my throne in the north, and I will be like the Most High. And in the Gospel: All these things will I give you, if falling down you will adore me.
2.7: 2.7 Then Holofernes. RABANUS, on the book of Judith, vol. 3. That Holofernes signifies the princes of the nations who persecuted the Church, etc., down to that all may adore the dragon who gave such power to the beast.
2.12: 2.12 And when he had passed. THE SAME, ibid. By the various provinces, and the names of places contained in the history, distinctions of persons and of ranks and dignities are designated, from which the devil claims some part for himself, nor fears the difficulty of the fight, but contends to bring about a great ruin of great power.
2.13: 2.13 And he plundered all. Taking away the usefulness of knowledge and the other things by which they ought to have served God: and converting them to the use of his service: he slew those who resisted with the edge of the sword, because those whom he cannot bend to consent he kills bodily.
2.17: 2.17 He went down into the plains. Damascus is interpreted drinking of blood, in which are expressed the princes of the nations, who thirst for the blood of the faithful: especially in the time of harvest, that is, at the consummation of the age, the fury of Antichrist raging through the breadth of the world.
3.1: 3.1 Then they sent, etc. The powerful of the world and lovers of pleasures, who strive to reconcile the prince of the world to themselves, that they may escape the danger of death and the loss of pleasure; of whom it is said: Whoever will be a friend of this world becomes an enemy of God. In these the care of this world and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and it bears no fruit; for these, according to the names of these provinces, are lifted up with pride, follow vanity: they enter the land by two ways, and will be joined to the company of mourners, or of those paying the penalties of their luxury, in hell: where they shall pass from the waters of snow to excessive heat, and their worm shall not die, and the fire shall not be quenched.
4.13: 4.13 Be mindful. He strengthens by the examples of the saints, hence Job chapter 12: You renew your witnesses against me, and Paul to the Hebrews, praising the virtue of faith, brought in abundant examples of the fathers, who by faith conquered kingdoms, wrought justice.
5.5: 5.5 Then Achior the leader, etc. As the prince of heretics, who, given to idolatry, who knew of divine works and miracles what he often tells others, although he has not perfectly learned the Catholic faith, and is not reborn by the baptism of Christ. Or by Achior are designated heretics, who although they do not hold the way of truth in all things, yet in their teaching preach many true things which agree with our faith. These fight against the Catholic Church, but overcome by reason they do not altogether conceal the truth, for heretics mix good with evil; because if they always said evil things they could not lie hidden; as he who offers a cup of poison touches the rim of the chalice with honey, that what is sweet may be tasted first, lest what is deadly be feared. Sometimes, however, corrected, they are saved, as Achior, seeing the victory of Judith, joined to the people of God, circumcised the flesh of his foreskin: the evangelical lepers also express heretics, who while they insert wrong things into right, as it were sprinkle a healthy color with blotches.
6.10: 6.10 Then the children of Israel coming down from Bethulia came. The sons: the teachers of the Church loose the one bound to the tree when they teach their catechumens to fear neither the rage of persecutors nor death. They loose him as bound to a tree when they rescue the fearful mind from the dread of the cross, and instruct it to suffer, but this is done better if, after the example of Ozias and Charmis, who comforting Achior poured out devout prayers to the Lord with all the people, the masters of the Church with the other faithful commend their hearers to the Lord with devout prayers, that by his gift may be had what human weakness does not deserve.
6.19: 6.19 And he made him a great supper. He makes it when the fast is ended, who refreshes a soul long languishing and needing the bread of the word of the Lord, with evangelical doctrine and the feasts of virtues. To this banquet are called all the priests, that by their exhortations and examples the neophytes may be strengthened to receive or preserve the faith.
7.7: 7.7 There were, however, fountains not far from the walls. As in the book of Kings the Philistines take away the blacksmiths, that they make not for the Hebrews either spear or sword. And all Israel went down to the Philistines to sharpen every man his plowshare, and his spade, and his axe, and his mattock. For this the devil especially strives, to take away the streams of doctrine and the arms of virtues, and so quickly accomplish his wickedness for the destruction of the servants of God: hence the princes of the nations and Julian the Apostate forbid Christians not only divine but also human philosophy.
7.12: 7.12 Then they gathered to Ozias. The carnal who say Lord, Lord, but their heart is far from me, Matthew 7, 15. For in the net of the Lord there are both good and bad fish, until the shore of the future judgment, who, bearing heavily the discomforts of the present life, prefer to use present delights than to have heavenly goods reserved for them in the future, who afflict their masters with importunate complaints and compel them to assent to the luxury of the world, whence it follows:
7.23: 7.23 And these five days, etc. The five days are the five senses of the body, by which the present life is led, as five days' truce the idle teacher seeks, who indiscreetly promises his hearers bodily comfort, as if the munificence of the supreme giver were in his power, when rather the time and manner of giving stand in the power of the giver rather than the receiver: for if the comfort of the present life is denied, they desert their subjects, that yielding to persecutions they may avoid bodily punishment. This agreement our Judith, that is the Church, rejects and despises.
8.1: 8.1 And it came to pass when, etc., there follows Daughter of Merari. That is of bitterness. For the Church through bitterness and tribulation is generated to the joys of the life to come: where she will praise the Lord forever. That she is narrated as descended in the fifteenth generation signifies that the Church through the hebdomad of the law and the ogdoad of the Gospel is brought forth from the patriarchs and apostles, and is to ascend to heavenly grace; hence this number of degrees is put in the Psalter, figurative of the future ascent to the heavens, by which the saints coming rightly say, Behold now bless the Lord.
8.2: 8.2 And her husband was Manasses, etc. Manasses is interpreted forgetful or necessity, to whom Judith was joined in marriage as if liable to the decalogue of the law or the rites of the Gentiles. But Christ coming and the light of the Gospel shining in the world, all that observance gave way, and as a cheap gathering of harvest quickly passed; hence the Apostle: But after the faith is come, we are no longer under a pedagogue. For you are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus, Galatians 3. And to the Romans he says: You also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ, that you may be another's, who is risen again from the dead, Romans 7. And the husband Manasses, Christ the bridegroom of the Church. He is well called Manasses, because he makes us forget our former calamity by the consolation of the life to come. This one in the time of the barley harvest, that is of the gathering of the Jewish people, when he sent his apostles to preach and gather the sheaves of believers: the heat of persecution came upon his head, that is upon his divinity. For the head of Christ is God, 1 Corinthians 11. Hence especially the Jews were scandalized, that he said he was the Son of God. Hence, You make yourself God, John 10. And elsewhere: Because he made himself the Son of God, ibid. 19. Jesus suffered among his own nation, and was buried in a garden. His bride, the bridegroom being taken away, gives herself to fasting and prayer, until the consummation of the age, nor deigns to be polluted by heretical errors. To whom her husband left the riches of spiritual wisdom and virtue: and gathered a household, that is a multitude of nations.
8.7: 8.7 To whom her husband had left great riches. From the instruction of the old law and of philosophy and moral discipline, the Church coming to Christ brought manifold wealth; hence Paul also glories that he was brought up at the feet of Gamaliel, and Moses is read to have been instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians.
8.12: 8.12 This is not the speech. When we are afflicted, we ought to prescribe to the Lord neither time nor manner, but rather leave everything to his judgment. Hence one of the fathers is read to have said in his prayer: Son of God, Son of God, as you know, and as you will, have mercy on me, Matthew 6. We ought only to seek the kingdom of God, and all things will be added. Let the present life be for the faithful in use, the future in fruit. Let the temporal thing be on the journey, let the eternal be desired in arrival.
8.28: 8.28 And they said. Whatever the Church speaks in the confession of faith in the doctrine of religion is laudable and irreproachable; this she warns each of the faithful beforehand by praying, if each, as he has proved true what he teaches, so fulfills it by works: hence it is added:
